title: Withdraw your Hyperliquid balance to your wallet
verified: Tested on a real account on 2026-10-27: following this guide, the amount that arrived matched the estimate to within 0.01 USDC.
covers: USDC in your account, and USDH that's no longer issued
summary: Still have USDC on Hyperliquid, or some USDH, a stablecoin that's no longer issued? Sell the USDH for USDC, then withdraw everything in one go to your wallet on Arbitrum.
facts: 1 USDC comes out of the withdrawal
About 10 minutes of steps; the withdrawal lands in about 5
Nothing. You don't need ETH on Arbitrum

support.label: Hyperliquid official support
support.note: Hyperliquid's docs say support only happens through a ticket in the open-ticket channel of its official Discord, or through its official email form. Any "support" that DMs you is a scammer.

pro: **Route**: USDH is no longer issued → sell it on spot for USDC with a limit order at {{floorPx}} or better → Withdraw to Arbitrum. 1 USDC fee, lands in about 5 minutes.
**Account mode**: unified accounts (the new default) withdraw directly. Older separate accounts first move spot USDC to Perps with Perps ⇄ Spot.
**Your numbers**: sell {{usdhSell}} USDH, withdraw {{withdrawAmt}} USDC, about {{arrive}} USDC arrives.
**Signatures**: 2–3 EIP-712 signatures, no gas. Check two things: the domain is app.hyperliquid.xyz, and destination is your own {{addrShort}}.
**Gotchas**: searching USDH also shows USDHL, so pick the right one. Tapping the order book on the right overwrites your price.

done.where: on the Arbitrum network in your wallet
done.look: Where to look: your wallet app → Assets → USDC → the Arbitrum line.

open.title: Open the official site in your wallet app
items: Open your wallet app (for example, the Wallet tab in the Binance app) and make sure the wallet holding these funds is the one selected.
Open `https://app.hyperliquid.xyz` in the wallet's built-in DApp browser. Include https://, or it gets treated as a search.
Once it loads, check the address bar: the domain must be exactly **app.hyperliquid.xyz**. One extra letter or a missing dot means it isn't the real site.
✗ If the page says your region can't use it (restricted jurisdiction), stop here. This guide doesn't cover getting around regional restrictions.

search-instead.see: Typing the address brings up search results
search-instead.do: Type the full address with https:// in front: `https://app.hyperliquid.xyz`.

restricted.see: The page says your region can't use it (restricted jurisdiction)
restricted.do: Stop here. This guide doesn't cover getting around regional restrictions.

not-sure.see: You're not sure it's the official site
not-sure.do: Check the address bar: the domain must be exactly **app.hyperliquid.xyz**. If it isn't, close the page and type the address yourself. Never use a link someone sent you.

connect.title: Connect your wallet
connect.note: Connecting only. No signature, and no money moves
images: ① Tap **Connect** in the top-right corner
① Choose **Default Wallet**. Your wallet asks to connect: if the request comes from app.hyperliquid.xyz, tap Connect
① Your address appears in the top-right (blurred here). It should be {{addrShort}} ② Tap the market name on the left to open the list

no-popup.see: You tapped Connect, but your wallet didn't ask to connect
no-popup.do: Open the page in your wallet app's built-in DApp browser (step 1). A regular phone browser can't reach your wallet.

wrong-address.see: The address in the top-right isn't the one holding the funds
wrong-address.do: Switch to the right wallet in your wallet app, then connect again. If the address doesn't match, don't go any further.

wrong-origin.see: The connection request doesn't come from app.hyperliquid.xyz
wrong-origin.do: Tap Reject and close the page. It may not be the official site.

search.title: Find the USDH market
search.whenText: Only needed if you have USDH (this step through step 6)
images: ① Type USDH in the search box ② Tap **USDH/USDC** (marked SPOT underneath) ✗ Don't tap USDHL/USDC: it's a different coin, one letter apart

two-results.see: Both USDH and USDHL show up
two-results.do: Pick **USDH/USDC**, the one marked SPOT. USDHL is a different coin; the names differ by one letter.

not-found.do: Check the spelling (U-S-D-H). Still nothing? Tap **All** to the right of the search box and search again.

panel.title: Open the sell panel and switch to a limit order
images: ! The yellow box is Hyperliquid's own notice: USDH is no longer issued, so buyers on this market will keep thinning out. The sooner you sell, the better
① Tap the small arrow next to **Market** in the top-left
① Choose **Limit** (a limit order only fills at your price or better)

no-limit.see: There's no Limit in the drop-down
no-limit.do: Tap the small arrow next to Market in the top-left, where the red box is in the screenshot above.

fill.title: Fill in the sell order
fill.note: Fill it in now; you'll enable trading next
images: ① Tap **Sell** ② Price: {{floorPx}} ③ Amount: {{usdhSell}} (the screenshot shows sample numbers) ④ Glance at Order Value: about {{orderMin}} USDC, the least you'll get ⑤ Tap **Enable Trading**
items: ! The green numbers on the right are other people's buy orders. You'll sell into them, usually at better than 0.995. **Don't tap them**: tapping one overwrites the price you entered.

value-off.see: Order Value is way off from the number here
value-off.do: The price or amount is probably wrong: price {{floorPx}}, amount {{usdhSell}}. If you tapped the green numbers on the right, your price was overwritten; enter it again.

not-enough.see: It says your balance isn't enough for that amount
not-enough.do: Some of your USDH may already be locked in an open sell order. The live check above shows how much you can actually sell. If you haven't added your address, add it above first.

place-order.see: The button already says Place Order, not Enable Trading
place-order.do: Trading was enabled before. Skip "Enable trading" and go straight to "Place the sell order".

enable.title: Enable trading
images: ① Leave **Stay Connected** unticked ② Tap **Establish Connection**. Your wallet asks for a signature: check it against the card below

check.title: Before you sign, check 3 things
check.lead: After you tap Establish Connection, your wallet shows a signature request. Compare it with this card and tick each line as you check it.

confirm.title: The request comes from app.hyperliquid.xyz
confirm.sub: One extra letter or a missing dot makes it a different site

confirm.title: It says ApproveAgent and Mainnet
confirm.sub: This creates a key that can only place orders. Hyperliquid's docs say it can't send money to anyone or withdraw

confirm.title: A signature only: no amount, no recipient
confirm.sub: Nothing is spent and no fee is charged

reject: It asks you to send money, or shows an amount
It mentions Permit, or approving (Approve) a token
normal: agentAddress is a random address that changes every time: it's the temporary order key the page creates
chainId may show 42161 or 56. Either is fine; it follows your wallet's current network
verifyingContract is all zeros. Also fine

no-approve-agent.see: The signature request doesn't mention ApproveAgent
no-approve-agent.do: Tap Reject. If the card doesn't match, don't sign.

no-change.see: You signed, but nothing changed on the page
no-change.do: Wait a few seconds. If the button still doesn't say Place Order, refresh the page, reconnect your wallet and tap Establish Connection again. Signing a second time is normal.

chain-id.do: That's normal. It follows your wallet's current network and changes nothing.

order.title: Place the sell order
order.note: Your wallet won't pop up for this one
items: Once you've signed, the page says Established connection, and the Enable Trading button turns into **Place Order**.
Check once more: Sell / price {{floorPx}} / amount {{usdhSell}} (enter them again if they were cleared).
Tap Place Order. If a Confirm Order box appears, check the same three things and confirm. The page's order key signs this one, so your wallet stays quiet.
When it fills, you should see an Order filled message. Under Balances, USDH drops to less than 0.01 and USDC goes up by about {{spotAfter}}. Open Orders is empty.
! If the order is still sitting under Open Orders, the bid has dropped below {{floorPx}}. Don't place another order. Tap "Stuck?" in the top-right for a live check.

resting.see: The order just sits there and doesn't fill
resting.do: The bid is below your price right now. Don't place another order. The live check above works out your options from today's bids.

too-small.see: It says the order is too small
too-small.do: Hyperliquid has a minimum order size (about $10). If your USDH is below that, it can't be sold. Leave it and go withdraw your USDC.

dust-left.see: A tiny bit of USDH is left under Balances after selling
dust-left.do: Amounts only go to two decimals, so less than 0.01 left over is normal. It doesn't affect the withdrawal.

transfer.title: Move your spot USDC to the perps account
transfer.whenText: Only for older separate accounts; unified accounts skip this
items: ! Check the Account page first. If the heading says **Unified Account Summary** and there are only Deposit / Withdraw buttons, you have a unified account: **skip this step** and go straight to the withdrawal.
images: ! If you see Unified Account Summary, it's a unified account (sample image; ignore the numbers)
A unified account only has Deposit / Withdraw: tap Withdraw and jump to the next step
Separate accounts show two lines, Spot and Perps: money in two accounts
① Tap **Account** at the bottom ② Tap **Perps ⇄ Spot**
① Tap this middle button to flip the direction

① Make sure it now reads Spot → Perps ② Tap **MAX** (the screenshot was taken before selling, so it shows 0.00; yours should be about {{spotAfter}}) ③ Tap **Confirm**. Your wallet asks for a signature: check it against the card

check.title: Before you sign, check 3 things
check.lead: After you tap Confirm, your wallet shows a signature request. Compare it with this card and tick each line as you check it.

confirm.title: The request comes from app.hyperliquid.xyz
confirm.sub: One extra letter or a missing dot makes it a different site

confirm.title: It says SendAsset, and destination is your own address {{addrShort}}
confirm.sub: Upper or lower case doesn't matter. If it isn't your address, reject it

confirm.title: From spot to perps, about {{spotAfter}} USDC
confirm.sub: sourceDex is spot and destinationDex is empty; the token is USDC:0x6d1e…e054

reject: It mentions Permit, or approving (Approve) a token
normal: It's a signature only, with no fee

no-button.see: There's no Perps ⇄ Spot on the Account page
no-button.do: If the heading says Unified Account Summary, it's a unified account. No transfer needed; go straight to the withdrawal.

max-zero.do: First make sure the direction is Spot → Perps (the middle button flips it). If it's still 0, there's no USDC left in spot; go straight to the withdrawal.

wrong-destination.see: The signature request shows a destination that isn't your address

withdraw.title: Withdraw to Arbitrum
images: ! Hyperliquid says the 1 USDC fee comes out of the withdrawal ① Leave the asset as USDC and the chain as Arbitrum ② Tap **MAX**: it should be about {{withdrawAmt}} (the screenshot shows a different number) ③ Tap **Withdraw to Arbitrum**. Your wallet asks for a signature: check it against the card

check.title: Before you sign, check 3 things
check.lead: After you tap Withdraw to Arbitrum, your wallet shows a signature request. Compare it with this card and tick each line as you check it.

confirm.title: The request comes from app.hyperliquid.xyz
confirm.sub: One extra letter or a missing dot makes it a different site

confirm.title: It says Withdraw, and destination is your own address {{addrShort}}
confirm.sub: If it isn't your address, reject it

confirm.title: amount is about {{withdrawAmt}}
confirm.sub: What arrives = this number minus the 1 USDC fee

reject: It mentions Permit, or approving (Approve) a token
normal: It's a signature only, with no gas: Hyperliquid sends the Arbitrum transaction for you
time is a 13-digit number. It's a timestamp

less-than-expected.see: MAX shows less than the number here
less-than-expected.do: Open orders and positions tie up part of your balance. The live check above lists where every part of your money is.

cannot-click.do: The withdrawal has to be more than the 1 USDC fee. Smaller amounts can't be withdrawn.

wrong-destination.see: The signature request shows a destination that isn't your address

check.title: Arrival check
rows: Your wallet app → Assets → USDC → the Arbitrum line
Sent from 0x2Df1…3dF7 (Hyperliquid's official bridge) to your address, as native Arbitrum USDC (0xaf88…5831)
After 30 minutes, don't withdraw again. Take a screenshot and ask us

not-in-wallet.see: You can't see the USDC in your wallet
not-in-wallet.do: Make sure you're looking at USDC on the **Arbitrum** network. The live check above looks up this withdrawal on Arbitrum directly.

one-less.do: That's the 1 USDC withdrawal fee. Normal.

late.see: It's been more than 30 minutes and nothing has arrived
late.do: Don't withdraw again. Look at the live check above. If it can't find the arrival, or it doesn't match, take screenshots to Hyperliquid's official support (below).
